The occupation code 29-1229.03 corresponds to urologists. They diagnose and treat genitourinary system and related adrenal problems; the US task profile describes the occupation, while practice in China depends on local qualifications, registration, and actual authorization.

Inputs include the patient's history, existing records, examination and test results, previous treatment information, and the patient's own request. The physician verifies the patient's identity, the timing of information, and inconsistencies, and cannot assume the facts are complete from one summary.

Explain the materials using professional knowledge, form a clinical judgment, and state the items to be confirmed; the specific plan is decided by a qualified physician according to clinical standards and the patient's situation. This page does not provide disease diagnosis or medication instruction.

Outputs include real medical records, explanations of examinations, treatment plans, and handover and follow-up records. Known facts, professional judgments, plans, and unfinished items must be distinguished, and a template or AI-generated text must not be treated directly as an action already carried out.

Outpatient assessment and the surgical perioperative period differ in materials, time points, and collaboration; updating records requires verifying the change in facts. Surgery, examinations, and equipment operation must be carried out under the corresponding training, institutional conditions, and authorization.

Collaborate with nursing, physicians in other specialties, resident physicians, and related staff; refer or request support when something exceeds your experience, expertise, or scope of practice. Each role's responsibility and handover still needs to be clear.

Beyond medical work, you may take part in teaching, research, and continuing education. Teaching or research achievements and clinical ability are assessed separately, and papers, research group positions, or academic activities are not equated with clinical practice authorization.

Material use must follow patient privacy, institutional management, and the corresponding authorization; real medical records must not be placed freely in a public portfolio. Applicants present their own real training experience and compliant learning outputs, without exaggerating surgical ability.

The work can be understood as two task lines: outpatient assessment and treatment, and surgery and perioperative collaboration. Both share material verification, professional judgment, patient communication, and records, but each clinical action depends on the actual patient, qualifications, and institutional arrangements. The following is an editorial summary at the occupational level, not a clinical operating procedure.

Traceable medical records, treatment arrangements, explanations, and follow-up information

How do outpatient care and perioperative work differ?

Both are clinical tasks within this occupation, but the input timing, team interfaces, and outputs differ. Outpatient work emphasises comprehensive assessment, explanation, and follow-up arrangements, while the perioperative period also requires the corresponding technical training, teamwork, and institutional authorization; a paper exercise cannot replace either clinical ability.

The work may involve medical institutions such as hospitals and clinics, surgery and examination settings, and may also include teaching and research. The US occupational context is background only; scheduling, training, qualifications, and authorization in China are verified with the actual organization.

Common organizations and locations | Outpatient clinics, wards, and related treatment areas in medical institutions; teaching and research have their own specific teams. Materials and tools | History, examination and test information, medical records, and the corresponding equipment; electronic records and office software assist recording and collaboration, are not evidence of AI adoption, and certainly do not automatically authorize operating instruments.

Clinical work is organized around real patients and institutional rules, and outpatient and perioperative tasks are arranged by specialty and position, so a uniform procedure cannot be applied; when authorization is unclear, verify it with the appropriate person in charge first.

Communicate with the patient, nursing, anaesthesia, and related specialties, keeping the facts and unfinished items in the handover, pointing out materials that cannot be confirmed in good time, and not treating a summary as confirmed by everyone.

Review and responsibility | Patient materials and clinical judgments require real verification, and physicians and the team bear care, record, and handover responsibility according to their duties. Qualifications, registration, institutional technical authorization, and actual ability are confirmed separately.

Quality and professional requirements | Observe whether records are true, whether judgments are well grounded, and whether the person can communicate clearly and acknowledge scope limits; training assessment is carried out by real education and clinical systems, and being right on paper on this page does not prove the ability to practise.
